SubTopics: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.
Content: Which of the following sentences from the passage `bbtext(best)` support the conclusion that all living organisms are part of the food chain?

A.Choice: “The energy you use to live every day travels from `text(one)` living thing to another, in a chain that starts with the sun.”

B.Choice: “This energy then helps plants change water from the soil and carbon dioxide from the air into oxygen and carbohydrates that power their cells.”

C.Choice: “Food chains everywhere-in grasslands and deserts, oceans and tropical rainforests - begin with the producers.”

D.Choice: “Scientists have been studying this isolated food chain for `50` `text(years)` to understand how changes in one link can cause changes in another.”

SubTopics: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.
Content: Read the sentence from the text.
:ibox:On Isle Royale - a small, `ultext(remote)` island in Lake Superior - wolves, moose, and balsam fir trees are bound together in a three-link food chain.
The word remote has multiple meanings. What does the word `ultext(remote)` `bbtext(most likely)` suggest about human contact with the island?

A.Choice: The island can only be reached by radio signals.

B.Choice: The island is an uncomfortable environment for humans.

C.Choice: The animals and plants on the island are rarely disturbed by humans because the island is isolated.

D.Choice: The animals and plants on the island bear little resemblance to the animals and plants humans usually encounter.

C.Choice: “`text(Ten)` times the size of a wolf, a moose has long, strong legs and a dangerous kick.”

D.Choice: “However, when the moose population decreases, wolves starve.”

Content: What are the `bbtext(most likely)` reasons the author included the section “Living Links” before the sections “Isle Royale: Predators, Prey, and Producers” and “Ups and Downs”? Select `bbtext(two)` options.

A.Choice: The section “Living Links” introduces carnivores, and carnivores are mentioned in the last `text(two)` sections.

SubTopics: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.
Content: A student is writing a story for class about camping. Read the draft of the story and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:`bbtext(Wilderness Getaway)`

Alexis and Simon would be leaving on a camping trip with family and friends later in the day. Simon did not know what to expect because he had never pitched a tent or stayed in one overnight. Alexis, however, had been camping many times and loved waking up with the sun and breathing the fresh morning air. She showed Simon pictures of roasting marshmallows and hot dogs over a large campfire. Alexis and Simon woke before dawn to help pack the camping supplies-a tent, hot dogs, graham crackers, chocolate, marshmallows, and sleeping bags.

Alexis, Simon, and their family and friends departed for the camping grounds at a nearby park. When they arrived, they searched for the perfect place to pitch the tent. Simon enjoyed the beautiful scenery. He was positive that he was going to have a great time at this getaway.
Choose the `bbtext(best)` sentence to add descriptive detail to paragraph two.

A.Choice: Alexis and Simon gathered dry wood for the campfire.

B.Choice: Simon and Alexis pitched their tents in an area shaded by trees.

C.Choice: Alexis enjoyed playing at the park and building a campfire to roast marshmallows.

D.Choice: Simon felt the soft earth beneath his feet and noticed the glassy lake near the campsite.

SubTopics: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
Content: A student is writing a report for her English teacher about beneficial relationships between people and animals. Read the draft of the introduction to the report and the directions that follow.

:ibox:The bond between people and animals has remained strong throughout history. In the past, tamed animals have helped humans with work such as hunting, farming, and transportation. More recently, animals have served people who are blind or have other disabilities. Today, people depend upon animals more for companionship than for work. One important benefit of such companionship for humans with pets is improved health.
The student took these notes from reliable sources:

:ibox:• Taking dog to dog park = chance to be with others
• Engaging with others = healthy mind
• Researchers studied people, pets more than `25` `text(years)`
• Strong relationship with pet = less stress
• Lowering stress = lower blood pressure
• Children with pets = fewer allergies to furry animals
• Dog owners who walk dogs healthier = walking is good exercise
• Taking care of a pet-walking, grooming, playing-helps a person think of others.
Using information from the student's notes, write `text(one)` paragraph developing the idea in the last sentence of the introduction.

SubTopics: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.
Content: A student is writing an argumentative letter to the principal about a plan to have students attend school during the summer months. Read the paragraphs from the draft of the student's letter and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:I am writing in opposition to your proposal to extend the school year. I also urge you to consider carefully recommendations from everyone who would be affected- staff, parents, the community, and especially students-before making your decision. With so many changes occurring in education, a hasty decision would do more harm than good.

`ultext(One reason I oppose your plan to extend the school year is that both students and parents are likely to oppose it.)` The students are the ones affected by this decision, and a survey by our school newspaper found that `76` `text(percent)` of them like our schedule as it is. I am a member of the newspaper staff, and I helped conduct the survey. These students are likely to influence their parents' views. If that happens, you will be bombarded with hundreds of emails and phone calls, insisting that kids are perfectly capable of learning without an extension of the school year. Your email inbox would fill up in a hurry. Even if parents agree with you, there's still the fact that when students are unhappy, their academic success rate goes down. That could undermine any additional learning achieved during the added time in class.
Choose the `bbtext(two)` sentences that should be removed from the second paragraph because they do not support the `ultext(underlined)` sentence.

A.Choice: The students are the ones affected by this decision, and a survey by our school newspaper found that `76` `text(percent)` of them like our schedule as it is.

B.Choice: I am a member of the newspaper staff, and I helped conduct the survey.

C.Choice: These students are likely to influence their parents' views.

D.Choice: If that happens, you will be bombarded with hundreds of emails and phone calls, insisting that kids are perfectly capable of learning without an extension of the school year.

E.Choice: Your email inbox would fill up in a hurry.

F.Choice: Even if parents agree with you, there's still the fact that when students are unhappy, their academic success rate goes down.

G.Choice: That could undermine any additional learning achieved during the added time in class.

Content: A student is writing a story for the school's online literary magazine. Read the draft of the story and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:`bbtext(Time Spent at the Lake)`

Martin visited his grandparents every summer near Round Lake. Typically, Martin refused to go fishing with his grandfather at the lake as he preferred to spend hours relaxing and reading books in the cool shade. The thought of sitting under the `ultext(very bright)` sun on a boat in the middle of the lake sounded like a boring waste of time. After `text(years)` of coaxing from his grandfather, however, Martin decided to attempt fishing. He listened intently to his grandfather's directions on how to cast the line of his fishing pole into the lake. Just seconds after his `text(first)` cast, Martin felt a sharp tug on his fishing line.
Choose `bbtext(two)` words that best replace the underlined words.

SubTopics: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general and their function in specific sentences.
Content: A student has written a paper for her English class about living in a rural area. Read the student's draft and complete the task that follows.

:ibox:Of the many advantages of country life over city life, my favorite is the opportunity to observe farm animals - especially pigs. Rolling in the mud, I like to watch them play. Myths about pigs abound, including the belief that they aren't very smart. My own observations confirm what scientific research has shown, namely, that pigs are highly intelligent and have very good memories. They can remember where food is hidden, recognize as many as `30` other pigs, and learned their names within a week of birth.

Another myth is that pigs are dirty and love to wallow in mud. They actually prefer water to mud. When people joke about “pigging-out,” they can't be talking about the animal because pigs eat slowly and savor their food. City folks could learn a lot by spending some time in the country.
Choose `bbtext(two)` sentences that contain errors in grammar usage.

A.Choice: Of the many advantages of country life over city life, my favorite is the opportunity to observe farm animals - especially pigs.

B.Choice: Rolling in the mud, I like to watch them play.

C.Choice: Myths about pigs abound, including the belief that they aren't very smart.

D.Choice: My own observations confirm what scientific research has shown, namely, that pigs are highly intelligent and have very good memories.

E.Choice: They can remember where food is hidden, recognize as many as 30 other pigs, and learned their names within a week of birth.

F.Choice: Another myth is that pigs are dirty and love to wallow in mud.

G.Choice: They actually prefer water to mud.

H.Choice: When people joke about “pigging-out,” they can't be talking about the animal because pigs eat slowly and savor their food.

I.Choice: City folks could learn a lot by spending some time in the country.

Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
Content: A student is writing a report about the history of computers. Read both sources and the directions that follow.

:ibox:`bbtext(Source 1: “The Speed of Computers” by Jonathan Anders)`

The `text(first)` computers were designed to solve math problems more quickly than a person could. Essentially, computers were invented to help people be faster with their work. For example, the United States takes a census of people living in the country to find out information about the population. The Census of `text(1880)` took about `text(eight years)` to complete; however, the `text(1890)` census took only `text(two years)`. This was because a machine was used to count the results of the `text(1890)` census. During the next `77` `text(years)`, devices like counting machines slowly changed to today's computers, which can do several jobs.

:ibox:`bbtext(Source 2: “How Computers Became Common in the Business World” by Hanna James)`

Before computers appeared in most offices, there were three machines that helped businesses conduct work at a faster pace: the typewriter, the filing system, and the adding machine. Since the `text(first)` computers were big machines that could only solve difficult math problems, it took time for them to be used in most offices. It took many inventors adding different capabilities to make computers what they are today. This eventually made it possible for offices to replace three machines with one. Nowadays people can solve math problems, type, copy, email, and save all from one device.
The student took notes about information in the sources. Which note correctly paraphrases, or restates, information from `bbtext(both)` sources?

A.Choice: Only companies with a lot of money could use the `text(first)` computers.

B.Choice: In modern times computers are commonly found in businesses, schools, and homes.

C.Choice: Throughout the `text(years)` computers have advanced to be able to do more tasks than they could before.

D.Choice: The `text(first)` computers were big machines designed to solve math problems more quickly than people can.

Content: A student is writing a research report about early sea navigation. She found a trustworthy source. Read the paragraph and the directions that follow.

:ibox:`bbtext(“Harrison's Marvelous Clock,” from The Story of Longitude by H. O. Bellevue, history Professor)`

Before the use of planes and trains became popular forms of transportation, many people relied upon boats to travel from one destination to the next. Sailors were a group of individuals who helped to guide and navigate boats. Before the `text(mid-1700s)`, there was not a dependable or practical way to determine a boat's east-west position, or longitude. Knowing a boat's longitude was essential to its safely reaching its destination. The key was being able to keep accurate time at sea. Although clocks kept the correct time on land, they did not work well on a rolling ship's deck. After years of effort, John Harrison of England invented the marine chronometer. The marine chronometer is a clock that allows a ship to determine its longitude at sea. Solving the longitude problem meant that ships could navigate more safely and accurate maps could be made. It is hardly an understatement to say that Harrison's success saved lives and continues to allow people to find their way around the world.
Choose `bbtext(two)` facts that support the author's point of view about Harrison's clock.

A.Choice: Tomorrow we shall arrive home from our voyage.

B.Choice: Like previous sailors, we could not figure our longitude accurately.

C.Choice: We navigated with charts of the moon and stars and big, bulky telescopes that were hard to use.

D.Choice: `text(Twice)` we ran into islands that our maps did not show.

E.Choice: Fortunately, injury to the ship was fixable.

F.Choice: We carried a clock, but it stopped working during a storm.

G.Choice: Finally, we were able to secure Mr. John Harrison's newest invention.

H.Choice: Because it kept nearly perfect time, we plotted our position most accurately and thus kept from running aground or worse.

I.Choice: This has made everyone on the ship very happy.

J.Choice: Now, our captain can draw updated maps that should be useful for sailors far into the future.
